prompt_rows.name: initial_search_instructions

prompt_rows.description:
1. Program 1 evaluates realizable balanced partitions using actor-weighted clique utility. Encode its exact cohort-count scan, population weights and tie handling, replacing the vague suggestion to optimize actual group sizes.
2. Program 1 combines a time-93 completion check with a time-95 hard cutoff. Encode its precise completion predicate: no unblocked partner is missing on either layer. Store the handoff permanently in separate Memory and apply it to both action and acceptance.
Program 1 reports 2.8459596 versus 2.8459563 for Programs 2–3. This tiny development difference supports testing the combined design, without establishing either change’s independent benefit. Preserve the simpler time-93 policy as a comparison and change one mechanism at a time.
prompt_rows.name: balanced_partition_completion

prompt_rows.description:
- All three leaders directly optimize actor-weighted utility across realizable balanced partitions. The rewrite makes this the structural baseline and specifies its singleton baseline and tie rules.
- The best program prioritizes overlapping ties within the sparser layer before considering the other layer. The rewrite specifies its two-pass reservoir sampling and random-draw behavior.
- Successful implementations combine persistent partner failure memory, permissive within-cohort acceptance, and precise rewiring cleanup. These behaviors are explicit, including their different effects on proposals and acceptance.
- Hard time-93 recovery and completion-aware extensions produce nearly equal scores. The rewrite separates timing experiments from partner-selection changes.
- Future changes must address a concrete behavioral bottleneck while preserving the selected parent’s unrelated behavior. Tiny development differences remain provisional.
prompt_rows.name: overlap_first_balanced_cohorts

prompt_rows.description:
- Extracted the strongest bundle: exhaustive utility-based degree selection, balanced actor-ID cohorts shared across layers, coordinated proposals and acceptance, layer balancing, persistent pruning, and failed-partner memory.
- Incorporated concrete implementation patterns: reservoir sampling, explicit action fallbacks, refreshed neighbors after rewiring, and policy state confined to supplied Memory.
- Preserved the best policy’s conditional construction window and late return to original behavior while treating its small measured advantage as uncertain.
- Added focused improvement hypotheses, including optimizing realized cohort sizes and revisiting persistent rejection memory, without claiming that individual components caused the observed gains.
prompt_rows.name: balanced_cohort_refinement

proposals.author_description: Combines balanced cohort construction with direct population-weighted partition optimization and a completion-aware recovery handoff. It retains the stronger simple partner sampling, shared failure memory, denser-layer pruning, and two-layer rewiring sequence. Cohort behavior runs from time 50 to 93, extends at most to time 95 only while an actor still has an eligible missing cohort link, and then permanently returns that actor’s actions and acceptance decisions to original behavior. This avoids the current program’s underperforming population-wide strong-incentive override while allowing nearly completed cohorts a short, bounded finishing window.

Replace uniform partner selection with one local ranking rule: prefer eligible cohort members already connected on the opposite layer, then maximize common within-cohort neighbors on the addition layer, reservoir-sampling ties. If no eligible overlap partner exists, preserve the original uniform selection and random-draw order. Count common neighbors only through permitted same-layer neighbor queries.
This may accelerate overlap and triangle formation before the unchanged time-93 recovery handoff. Acceptance, failure memory, cohort targets and pruning remain unchanged, including consent to finite negative-gain cohort offers. The risk is concentrating construction around existing clusters while delaying other links. This is an untested hypothesis; support requires improved full-panel terminal utility, assessed across the 36 history families with actor-level losses retained.

Shorten the shared cohort-construction window from time 95 to time 93 while preserving every other mechanism. This switches both action and acceptance back to original behavior together, giving the completed cohort structures seven terminal rounds for decentralized cleanup and adaptation. The saved evidence identifies the hard time-93 handoff as the strongest evaluated timing variant, while the current time-95 policy scores slightly lower.

novelty.novelty_explanation: **NOVEL**: The construction-phase cutoff changes from `95.0` to `93.0`. For `93.0 <= time < 95.0` with `triangleBenefit() >= 0.4`, the proposed code uses original turn and acceptance behavior instead of cohort-based rules. This timing hyperparameter change can alter network evolution and outcomes; all other logic is unchanged.

proposals.author_description: Replace contiguous actor-ID intervals with balanced round-robin cohorts defined by `actor % cohortCount`. The optimized cohort count, overlap-first partner sampling, failure memory, acceptance gate, action sequencing, and paired cleanup remain unchanged. This tests whether dispersing cohort members across actor IDs improves construction and recovery while preserving the exact optimized cohort-size distribution.

When total layer degrees tie, choose the layer with more eligible cohort partners already connected on the opposite layer. Exclude self and remembered failures, and retain layer 0 when counts tie. The counting step consumes no randomness; existing reservoir sampling remains unchanged.
This targets recovery states where external ties or failed partners make equally populated layers offer different overlap opportunities. It may accelerate spillover accumulation during cohort construction. Partner selection remains uniform within the chosen layer’s eligible pool, so overlap is not guaranteed. The change could also delay useful triangle closure. Partition arithmetic, acceptance, pruning, memory and phase transitions retain their current behavior.
This proposal is unevaluated. Improvement requires an authorized full-panel comparison, assessed across the 36 history families and available shocked/unshocked outcomes.
